history_facts.text: Seiko states its first Alpinist was the 1959 Seiko Laurel Alpinist, made for mountain climbers and recreational field sports, and the first Seiko watch made with sports in mind.

The 1959 original had a screw-back case against dust/sand, a leather cuff band against sweat, luminous hands/markers, and mountain-shaped markers at 3, 6, 9, 12 that double as the four compass points.

Seiko Germany's 2020 press release says Japanese mountaineers were called 'Yama-otoko', which gave the watch its name, and that the first models had a simple 17-jewel hand-wound calibre and black or white dials.
Seiko Germany (2020) says the Alpinist had been reissued six times since 1961 and that the 'Green Alpinist' SARB017 became a collector's piece.
Seiko France (Oct 2020) states the Alpinist joined Prospex in 2020, bearing the Prospex 'X' logo.
Seiko Italy (2025) says the green-dial version first appeared in 1995, was updated in 2006, and was nicknamed 'Green Alpinist' in Japan.
Seiko's 2026 Alpinist page says the Laurel Alpinist of 1959 was Seiko's first sports watch, and that the 2025 6R55 models put the Alpinist logo under the Seiko logo at 12 o'clock, as on the original.
The 6R55 Alpinist Mechanical models SPB503/505/507 were available from November 2025 (Seiko US special page).
From 2026, new Prospex references use an 'HBC' prefix (e.g. HBC006 Alpinist, HBC007 Alpinist GMT); in Japan the same number takes a 'J' suffix (HBC006J).
The 1959 Alpinist Re-creation SJE085 went on sale in Japan on 6 August 2021 at ¥330,000 (per Impress Watch).

disputes.note: Both are Seiko documents. Seiko's later global releases (2021, 2025) use 1959.
The product spec pages (39.5/13.2) are likely more reliable than the German press text.

unresolved: SPB197: a retailer (Watchnation) lists 'SPB197J1 2021 European Limited Edition', but Seiko's ES page names SPB201J1 as the 2021 European LE (2,021 pcs). No Seiko page for SPB197 found, so it is excluded from models[].

'Bamboo forest' Alpinist: the only match is SPB435 'Save the Forest – Bamboo Grove' (Thailand, 1,000 pcs, ~2023), documented only by retailers and Bangkok Post (paywalled). No Seiko-hosted page found. 'Sunbeam Forest' (SPB210) and 'Mystic Forest' (SPB289) are retailer nicknames.
'Alpinist Snow': the closest match is SPB532 'Snowy Mountain' (SE Asia LE, 800 pcs). No Seiko-hosted source found.
Deep Lake / Forest Brown dial stories come from retailer copy (likely Seiko UK marketing text); no Seiko-hosted wording found.
JP refs for SPB117/119/121 (SBDC087/089/091) are matched by colour and strap from press; SBDC089 is called 'cream' by Hodinkee Japan vs SPB119 'silver'.
JP refs for the 38mm and 1959-series models were not verified (SBDC117 is likely SPB157; retailers say SPB211 = SBDC137).
Movement entry for 6R15 not verified against Seiko this pass.
